subject: Orion Systems — perf triage + A/B actions
messages:
From: Ethan Miller <ethan.miller@orionsys.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-12T15:03:00-07:00
Subject: Quick follow-up on today's latency/throughput runs

Thanks again for the call this morning — good to get aligned. We ran a quick informal A/B between Redwood's hosted inference and HyperCloud's inference API using our standard conversational workload (mixed prompts, median seq length ~256 tokens). High-level notes from our side: 

- Redwood: p95 ~ 220ms lower than HyperCloud for short seqs (<=128), tokens/sec ~ 1.35x higher at batch size 8.
- HyperCloud: slightly better cold-start for very large seqs (>1024) in our runs, p99 comparable but more variance.
- We saw some CDN/network spikes in one of the racks during the HyperCloud runs (I've captured the raw logs).

We need to formalize this into a repeatable A/B so procurement and engineering can compare apples-to-apples. Can you confirm:
- exact model binary/config you used (model name, quantization, sequence length truncation)
- the endpoint config (batching policy, max_tokens, KV cache behavior)

I've attached the raw logs and a short baseline CSV. Also attaching our internal decision criteria: procurement will weight 1) p95 latency 2) throughput/$ 3) stability.

[Attachment: orion_raw_logs_20270912.tar.gz (tar.gz, 8.2MB)]
[Attachment: orion_baseline_q3.csv (CSV, 28KB)]

Thanks,
Ethan
Ethan Miller
SRE Lead, Orion Systems
ethan.miller@orionsys.com
+1 (415) 555-0189

From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Miller <ethan.miller@orionsys.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-12T16:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up on today's latency/throughput runs

Appreciate the summary and the logs, Ethan — useful data. We've looked through the CSV and spot-checked the tar logs. Quick recap from our side and a proposed A/B protocol so results are reproducible: 

Summary (what we saw so far):
- On our hosted endpoints we used model: rdx-7b-chat-v1 (quantized int4 in the experiment you observed).
- Default endpoint config: dynamic batching with max_batch_delay=10ms, max_batch_size=16, KV cache enabled for streaming tokens.
- For short sequences (<=128) our continuous-batching path amortizes overhead and gives the tokens/sec win you saw.

Proposed formal A/B protocol (3 controlled runs each side):
1) Model parity: run both vendors on rdx-7b-chat-v1 (we'll supply a containerized hash of the model weights/manifest to ensure parity).
2) Quantization parity: int4 vs int8 runs (two separate passes).
3) Batch sweep: batch sizes [1, 4, 8, 16] measuring p50/p95/p99 and tokens/sec.
4) Tail analysis: 1000-run tail (capture p99.9 and variance) and network latency breakdown.
5) Cost normalization: compute tokens/sec per $ at current quoted rates (we'll publish our cost calc).

Data to exchange: raw traces, perf profiles (nvprof/tensorboard snapshots if possible), and exact endpoint configs. Upload to the Drive folder I created: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB2cDefGhIJk-orion-perf — I dropped a test-config.yaml template you can use.

I'll attach the test-config.yaml with our recommended flags (batching window, warmup steps, sequence sampling). Proposed timeline: baseline runs by Sep 15, cross-vendor A/B by Sep 18, recap call week of Sep 20. If that works for you, we'll schedule the runbook and assign owners.

[Attachment: test-config.yaml (YAML, 2KB)]

Next steps (action items):
- Ethan: confirm you can run the template and upload traces to Drive by Sep 15.
- Ben: we'll prepare the containerized model artifacts and a deterministic seed for sampling.
- Marcus: I'll loop you on cost calc and can run a quick throughput/$ sheet once we have raw numbers.

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-12T17:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Orion Systems — perf triage + A/B actions

Quick note from infra: we should insist on identical model binaries (checksum). The biggest variance we've seen in prior A/Bs comes from subtle tokenizer pre-processing and kv-cache warmup policies. Two short asks for Orion's runbook: 

- Provide the exact prompt pre-processing script (we have a diff tool to compare tokenization buckets).
- Provide network topology (are their agents in the same cloud region as the Redwood endpoints?) — if they're testing from an on-prem client that hops through a CDN we need to isolate that.

I'll coordinate the container and seed Irene mentioned. Also, Marcus — I recommend we add a small experiment to disable continuous batching to measure pure single-request latency (helps procurement see worst-case p99).

Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
